title: 日米欧の中銀、介入後の円安占う「運命の6月」　利上げ理論が日銀縛る？
extracted_text:
原油高の再燃が円安に弾みをつけ、日本の財務省が円買い介入で応戦した。中東緊迫後の市場は新たな段階に入った。介入効果の持続性と今後の市場を占う意味で、焦点は日米欧の中央銀行が「運命の6月」にどう臨むのかだ。利上げに積極的なタカ派のアピールでは日銀が一歩先んじたようにもみえるが、現実はそう単純ではない。

「ビハインド・ザ・カーブ（利上げが後手に回る事態）に陥らない」ための精緻な論理展開そのものが日銀の判断を縛り、利上げに動きにくくなる。そんな意外かつ皮肉なリスクもひそんでいる。

日銀、米連邦準備理事会（FRB）、欧州中央銀行（ECB）は4月末にかけて開いた会合でそろって政策金利の据え置きを決め、総じて市場の反応も薄かった。ポイントを絞って分析しよう。

4月28日、日銀の金融政策決定会合。執行部の据え置き方針に民間出身の審議委員の半数にあたる3人が1.0%への利上げを唱え反対票を投じた。タカ派の代表格、高田創氏と田村直樹氏の投票行動は想定どおり。BOJ（日銀）ウオッチャーの間で驚きが広がったのは、執行部に寄り添う姿勢が強かった中川順子氏が退任を6月末に控えて反旗を翻し、「タカ派デビュー」を果たしたことだ。

次にパウエル議長が率いる最後の会合だったであろう4月29日の米連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）。据え置き方針に対し、いつもどおりにトランプ米大統領からの刺客であるミラン理事が0.25%の利下げを求めた。

注目は3人の地区連銀総裁が声明にある先行きの政策運営に関する「緩和バイアス」の表記に反対したことだ。緩和バイアスとは、昨年の利下げ局面から続く「さらなる政策金利の調整の幅とタイミングを検討するに当たり」という表現に込めた「次にアクションをとるとしたら利下げ」というニュアンスを指す。

そして30日のECB理事会。ラガルド総裁は記者会見で据え置きが「全会一致」だったと強調し、政策決定では唯一、何の波乱もなかった。

実態はどうなのか。最大のポイントは、利上げ票が3票に達した日銀と、全会一致で据え置いたECBのどちらが利上げに近いとみるのかだ。

ラガルド氏の会見に戻ろう。会合では「利上げの可能性についても時間をかけてじっくりと議論した」と明かした。次回会合までの6週間は「検証され、再検討された情報に基づき十分に検討された決定をくだすのに適切な期間となる」と語った。

日銀と違い、ECBはさまざまな経済や物価状況を抱える国の集まりだ。異なる意見を十分に聞いたうえでの「ワンボイス（統一見解）」に重きを置く傾向がもともとあった。「何でもやる」発言で有名になったドラギ総裁の時代はトップダウン型になびいたが、 第一ライフ 資産運用経済研究所の首席エコノミスト、田中理氏は「ラガルド体制はコンセンサス（合意）を重視する傾向がある」と指摘する。

ラガルド氏の発言からは、全会一致の据え置きの裏ですでに利上げ議論が白熱し、新たなスタッフ見通しがまとまる6月会合で結論を出そうという空気が伝わる。田中氏も「中東の問題が抜本的に解決しない限りは6月に利上げに動くとみるほうが自然ではないか」との見立てだ。

反対票の多寡では利上げへの距離感は測れない。6月利上げへの伏線の張り方は、ECBのほうが具体的だともいえる。

もちろん日銀も6月利上げの線を消していない。植田和男総裁は会見で物価の上振れリスクに対する警戒を強調し、「ビハインド・ザ・カーブに陥ることがないよう、次回以降の決定会合において適切に政策を判断していきたい」と踏み込んだ。

4月の「経済・物価情勢の展望（展望リポート）」でも利上げへの理論武装を精緻に組み上げた。1月の前回リポートでは円安を軸に輸入物価の上昇が国内物価の基調にまで及ぶ姿を描き、「インフレファイター」化への理論的な整理をすませた。今回、さらに原油高も踏まえて分析を進めた。

ただし、つぶさに確認すると、原油高との関連でビハインド・ザ・カーブのリスクが高まったと認定するハードルはそれほど低くないとわかる。

展望リポートで注目のテーマを集中的に扱う「BOX欄」では、原油高が経済に与える影響を分析し、「先行き景気が減速し、企業収益も減益となる可能性が高いとみられる中で、賃金上昇率が大幅に加速し、そのことがさらなる物価上昇率の高まりにつながる可能性は高くない」と指摘した。原油高が持つ賃金や物価全般に対する二次的波及効果は「円安ショックのほうが大きくなっている」という知見も盛り込んだ。

植田氏は利上げの前提に景気の下押しが一定程度にとどまることを挙げる。分析に照らすと、原油高が物価の押し上げに作用しても、しばらくは景気に目をこらさねばなるまい。6月に利上げを決断するとなれば、原油高というよりも、やはり円安に突き動かされる側面が強いだろう。

「ウォーシュFRB」の船出も焦点だ。6月会合は、次期議長候補として上院本会議の採決を待つのみになったウォーシュ氏が初陣を飾るであろう重要な場になる。

緩和バイアスの文言をどう扱うか。パウエル現議長は「新たなリーダーシップが重要な役割を果たす」とウォーシュ氏に委ねたが、当のウォーシュ氏は議会公聴会で事前に政策の方向性を示すコミュニケーションのあり方に拒否反応を示した。いっそのこと声明から削ってしまおうと動くかもしれない。

一気にハト派シフトを唱える可能性も低いだろう。公聴会では「物価安定こそがFRBが独立性を確立する道」という旨の持論を繰り返し、「インフレの軌道は改善しているが、まだやるべきことは残っている」とも語った。

持論とされた人工知能（AI）による生産性向上が利下げを可能にするとの見方には「AIに関するストーリーをそのようにはとらえていない」と軌道修正を図った。

こうみると、日米欧のなかで日銀のタカ派姿勢が埋没した状況を一気に挽回するのは難しいかもしれない。介入後も円安は底流でくすぶり続けそうだ。たとえ高市早苗政権があからさまな圧力をかけなくても、景気を慎重に見極め、円安進行に追い込まれてようやく利上げに動く――。中東緊迫前からさほど変わらぬ日銀の姿がみえる。

translated_text:
Rising crude oil prices have reignited yen weakness, and Japan's Ministry of Finance has responded with yen-buying interventions. The market has entered a new phase following Middle East tensions. In terms of the sustainability of intervention effects and forecasting the market's future direction, the focus is on how the central banks of Japan, the US, and Europe will approach the "fateful June." While hawkish advocates pushing for rate hikes appear to have put the Bank of Japan ahead, the reality is not that simple.

The meticulous logical framework developed to avoid "falling behind the curve" is itself constraining the BOJ's decision-making, making it harder to act on rate hikes. Such an unexpected and ironic risk also lurks in the shadows.

The Bank of Japan, the US Federal Reserve (FRB), and the European Central Bank (ECB) all decided to keep policy interest rates unchanged at their meetings held toward the end of April, and the market's reaction was generally subdued. Let me zero in on the key points.

April 28: BOJ Policy Board meeting. Against the Board's decision to hold rates, three of the five private-sector board members—half of the board—voted against the decision, advocating a rate hike to 1.0%. The votes cast by hawkish representatives Takashi Takada and Naoki Tamura were as expected. What surprised BOJ watchers was that Junko Nakagawa, who had typically aligned with the management side, flipped against the Board just before her term ends in June, marking her "hawkish debut."

Next, the April 29 FOMC meeting—the last meeting chaired by Chair Powell. Against the hold decision, Trump-installed Governor Milan, as always, pushed for a 0.25% rate cut.

The spotlight was on three regional Fed presidents opposing the inclusion of "easing bias" language in the statement regarding future policy guidance. Easing bias refers to the nuance embedded in last year's rate-cut phase expression—"when considering the scope and timing of further policy rate adjustments"—that the next action would be a rate cut.


Then, on April 30, the ECB Governing Council meeting. President Christine Lagarde emphasized at her press conference that the decision to hold was "unanimous," and it was the only policy decision with no turbulence.

But what is the reality? The key point is whether to view the BOJ, where rate-hike votes reached three, or the ECB, which unanimously held rates, as being closer to a rate hike.

Returning to Ms. Lagarde's press conference: she revealed that the meeting included "thorough discussions taking time on the possibility of rate hikes." The six weeks until the next meeting would be "an appropriate period to make a well-considered decision based on information that will be verified and reconsidered."

Unlike the BOJ, the ECB is a gathering of countries with diverse economic and price conditions. It has traditionally placed weight on reaching a "one voice" (unified view) after fully hearing differing opinions. During former President Mario Draghi's era, known for his "whatever it takes" statement, it leaned toward top-down governance, but Chief Economist Tanaka Akira from Daiwa Life Investments Research Institute noted that "the Lagarde administration tends to emphasize consensus."

From Ms. Lagarde's remarks, despite the unanimous hold vote, discussions on rate hikes are already heating up, and the atmosphere is to reach a conclusion at the June meeting when new staff projections come together. Mr. Tanaka also observed: "Unless issues in the Middle East are fundamentally resolved, wouldn't it be more natural to expect a rate hike in June?"

The number of dissenting votes cannot measure the distance to rate hikes. The way ECB has laid the groundwork for June rate hikes could be seen as more specific.

Of course, the BOJ hasn't ruled out June rate hikes either. Governor Kazuyoshi Ueda emphasized alertness to upside risks to prices at his press conference, stating, "We will appropriately judge policy at future meetings so as not to fall behind the curve."

The April "Outlook for Economic and Price Conditions (Outlook Report)" also built up a refined theoretical case for rate hikes. In the January report, it had framed yen weakness as driving imported price increases to affect domestic price fundamentals, completing a theoretical整理 of becoming an "inflation fighter." This time, it further incorporated analysis factoring in higher crude oil prices.


However, upon closer examination, the threshold for认定 that the Crude oil price surge has increased the risk of falling behind the curve is not that low.

The "BOX" section that intensively addresses key themes in the Outlook Report analyzes crude oil price impacts, noting: "With prospects for economic slowdown and corporate earnings likely to decline, it's unlikely that wage growth will accelerate significantly enough to lead to further price increases." It also incorporates the finding that secondary spillovers from crude oil prices on wages and general prices are "becoming larger than the yen shock impact."

Governor Ueda cites a certain level of economic downward pressure as a prerequisite for rate hikes. Based on this analysis, even if crude oil prices push prices up, we'll need to keep a close eye on the economy for some time. If deciding on a June rate hike, the driving force would more likely be yen weakness rather than crude oil prices.


The "Warsh Fed" launch is also in focus. The June meeting will be an important venue where Mr. Warsh, now waiting for the Senate floor vote as the next chair candidate, will make his debut.

How to handle easing bias language. Current Chair Powell left it to Warsh, noting "new leadership will play an important role," but Warsh himself has shown reluctance during congressional hearings to pre-commit to policy direction. He might move to just remove it from the statement altogether.

The likelihood of suddenly shifting to doveish rhetoric is also low. In hearings, he repeated his belief that "price stability is the path for the FRB to establish independence," adding, "The inflation trajectory is improving, but there's still work to be done."

He corrected course on the view that AI-driven productivity gains could enable rate cuts, saying he "doesn't see the AI story that way."

Given this, it may be difficult for the BOJ's hawkish stance to suddenly recover lost ground among Japan-US-Europe. Even after interventions, yen weakness seems likely to continue smoldering beneath the surface. Even without overt pressure from a Sanae Takaichi administration, we see the BOJ remaining largely unchanged from before the Middle East tensions—carefully monitoring the economy and only moving to raise rates when pushed by yen weakness progression.
title_en: Central Banks of Japan, US, Europe Forecast Yen Weakness Post-Intervention as 'Fateful June' — Do Rate Hike Theories Constrain the BOJ?
